reasons: CONDITIONAL is the right stance. Reach (state licence list, 290 homes), current demand (signal 2026-11-19), Brain-produced spreadsheet fulfilment, $4 cost, $0 exposure and 5-day settlement are on the card as evidence. The $600 price is one director's word on a call (PERSON), so price and close rate are both unknown, and the plan says so. A zero-cost priced offer to 40 homes measures both. I recomputed: 4 x $600 = $2,400. Delivery costs $16, paid out of settled fees. The receipt invoiced on day 14 settles on day 19, inside the 30 days. If even 1 of 40 closes, 290 homes yield about 7 sales, which is at least the 4 needed, so the proof threshold is coherent. The stop rules come before the window closes.

The card records 1 human hour per deal and no plan step accounts for it (owner hours are unstated, so it does not breach a limit)
